servingNote: 4 oz cooked (113 g), the USDA reference amount for cooked meat.

baseline.note: Eshel et al. 2014 (PNAS): US animal products use ~3.7 million km², beef ~88% of it (pasture 79 pts, processed roughage 7, concentrates 2). Beef = 0.88 x 3.7M = 3.256M km²; pasture share = 79/88. Data are 2000-2010 USDA averages, corrected for trade.
baseline.crossCheck: USDA ERS Major Land Uses 2022: 784.1 million acres (3.17 million km²) of grazing land, all livestock.

driSource: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets (RDA/AI tables); protein RDA from National Academies DRI tables.

consumption.source: USDA ERS Meat Supply and Disappearance Tables, updated 2026-09-29

replacementMethod: Replacement land = shift x baseline beef land x (plate land / beef-serving land), both per-serving lands from Poore & Nemecek 2018 global means per 100 g protein. P&N mean beef x 2025 US retail beef (9.18 Mt) = 3.0M km², close to Eshel, so the ratio transfers.
